symptom: `describe entity` of an entity with an index on its changedDate system member (Siemens FSM template 9.24.2, ten entities) printed `index ( desc);`, which `check` refuses ("index on unknown attribute 'desc'"), so every statement referencing the entity failed with it (mendixlabs/mxcli#1401).
cause: Not a dangling pointer: a system-member index segment is stored as DomainModels$IndexedAttribute.Type = ChangedDate/CreatedDate, with no attribute behind AttributePointer. The sdk IndexAttribute had no Type, indexFromGen dropped it, the describer resolved the column by attribute ID only (empty name, then ` desc`), the create/alter paths silently dropped or refused a `ChangedDate` column, and indexToGen hard-coded Type Normal — so any rewrite of such an entity (even `alter entity … set comment`) turned the index into an attribute segment pointing at nothing.
file: sdk/domainmodel/domainmodel.go (IndexAttribute.Type); mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel.go (indexFromGen) and domainmodel_write.go (indexToGen); mdl/executor/cmd_entities.go (systemIndexMemberType, newSystemIndexSegment, indexSegmentName, reconcileDroppedIndexes); mdl/executor/cmd_entities_describe.go
insight: Before choosing between 'skip it' and 'resolve it' for a pointer that resolves to nothing, look in the gen type for a discriminator: IndexedAttributeType's CreatedDate/ChangedDate values (modelsdk/gen/domainmodels/enums.go) answered what the stored index holds without a Studio Pro fixture, and the repro (`ChangedDate: AutoChangedDate` next to the empty column) pointed at it. The semantic struct had narrowed the enum to a constant, so the read side lost it and the write side reinvented 'Normal' — the rewrite-drops-unauthored-state class, live on every entity rewrite, not only on describe. MDL spells the column as describe declares the member (`index (ChangedDate desc)`); the names are MDL020-reserved for attributes so they cannot collide. Verified on a blank 11.6.6 app: exec → mx check 0 errors, describe → check → re-exec Unchanged, unrelated alter keeps the index, describe → exec on a fresh copy → identical describe. A segment that resolves to neither now describes as a `-- index skipped` comment on its own line, so the statement still parses. Studio Pro's exact AttributePointer bytes for such a segment were not observed (no fixture holds one); mxcli writes the all-zero GUID it already uses for the sibling AssociationPointer, which mx check accepts.
